cues.en: Instructor: In this video, I'm going to introduce you to independent components analysis, often abbreviated as ICA.
cues.zh: 講師：這支介紹獨立成分分析，縮寫 ICA。

cues.en: Similar to the previous lecture on PCA, the math for ICA is not super-duper difficult, but it does require a little bit more time to get into,
cues.zh: 像上一堂 PCA，數學不是非常難，但需要更多時間，

cues.en: to fully explain.
cues.zh: 才能完整解釋。

cues.en: So instead, what I'm going to do here is give you a simplified overview of one of the ICA algorithms.
cues.zh: 所以簡化概述其中一個 ICA 演算法。

cues.en: And in fact, ICA starts from the central limit theorem.
cues.zh: ICA 其實從中央極限定理開始。

cues.en: So you'll remember the central limit theorem, which is basically the idea that all roads lead to Gauss.
cues.zh: 記得，基本上就是條條道路通高斯。

cues.en: This is a picture of Gauss, apparently I never met him, but the internet says that this is Carl Gauss.
cues.zh: 這是高斯照片，沒見過他，但網路說這是 Carl Gauss。

cues.en: So independent components analysis starts from the idea, the assumption, that signals are non-Gaussian-distributed
cues.zh: ICA 假設訊號是非高斯分布，

cues.en: and mixtures of signals, random mixtures of signals, are Gaussian-distributed.
cues.zh: 而隨機混合訊號是高斯分布。

cues.en: And we know that that second condition, that assumption is correct because of the central limit theorem.
cues.zh: 中央極限定理告訴我們，第二個假設正確。

cues.en: So from the perspective of ICA, when we see a Gaussian distribution, we say, "Well, that's bad.
cues.zh: 從 ICA 角度，看到高斯分布就說：「不好。

cues.en: Gaussian distributions are either noise or they are random mixtures of signals."
cues.zh: 不是雜訊，就是隨機混合訊號。」

cues.en: So what we need to do is figure out a way to pull the data across different features of the dataset
cues.zh: 要找方式，把資料集不同特徵彙整，

cues.en: in order to make the weighted combinations of the features look as least Gaussian-distributed as we possibly can.
cues.zh: 讓特徵加權組合盡可能不像高斯分布。

cues.en: So it gets rid of as much of the Gaussianity in the dataset as possible.
cues.zh: 盡可能移除高斯性。

cues.en: So my apologies to Sir, or Dr. Professor Gauss, but that's basically what ICA starts from.
cues.zh: 對高斯爵士、博士、教授致歉，但這是 ICA 起點。

cues.en: By the way, it turns out that everything you need to know about how most, or some of the ICA algorithms work you've already learned in this course,
cues.zh: 多數或某些 ICA 演算法需要的知識，其實課程已學過。

cues.en: we can measure the Gaussianity of a distributions through, for example, kurtosis, which is the fourth statistical moment that you learned about
cues.zh: 例如可以用峰度，衡量分布高斯性，這是第四統計動差，

cues.en: in the section on Descriptive Statistics.
cues.zh: 在描述統計學過。

cues.en: Anyway, what I'd like to do now is first show you an example of how signals can have non-Gaussian distributions and how they can sum together
cues.zh: 先展示訊號如何非高斯，以及如何相加，

cues.en: to create a Gaussian distribution.
cues.zh: 形成高斯分布。

cues.en: Now, you've already seen some of this in slides and in action in the section on Probability Theory in the lectures about the central limit theorem.
cues.zh: 機率論、中央極限定理的投影片與實作，已看過一些。

cues.en: So here, we have some signals, and here we have their histograms.
cues.zh: 這些是訊號，以及直方圖。

cues.en: So you can see these are definitely non-Gaussian-distributed.
cues.zh: 肯定不是高斯分布。

cues.en: Now, you can imagine computing the kurtosis of these distributions.
cues.zh: 可以想像算這些分布的峰度。

cues.en: The kurtosis, remember, is the fatness of the tails.
cues.zh: 記得，峰度是尾部肥厚程度。

cues.en: So a perfect Gaussian distribution has, you know, little kurtosis or some specified amount of kurtosis because the tails are relatively small.
cues.zh: 完美高斯的峰度很小，或某個特定值，因為尾部相對小。

cues.en: So then we look at...
cues.zh: 接著看。

cues.en: In fact, all of the tails for all these distributions are much, much fatter than you would expect for a true Gaussian distribution, right?
cues.zh: 全部分布的尾部，都比真正高斯預期肥厚得多，對吧？

cues.en: So this is an extreme, a true Gaussian distribution that should be thin at the tails.
cues.zh: 真正高斯，尾部應該很細。

cues.en: And here, it's fatter at the tails than it is in the center.
cues.zh: 這裡尾部甚至比中央胖。

cues.en: Okay, so then what we do is sum up all of these data together, all these channels together, and the distribution of the sums of those channels
cues.zh: 把所有資料、通道加總，加總後的分布，

cues.en: is Gaussian approaches the Gaussian.
cues.zh: 是高斯，或趨近高斯。

cues.en: So now, the ICA will approach this distribution and say, "No, no, no, this is not good," and it's gonna come up with different ways of picking apart the signal
cues.zh: ICA 會說：「不好」，嘗試拆開訊號，

cues.en: and weighting together the different channels or the different features of your dataset in order to maximize the amount of kurtosis
cues.zh: 把不同通道或特徵加權，盡量增加各成分的峰度，

cues.en: or non-Gaussianity in each of the components that sum together to create this signal.
cues.zh: 或非高斯性；這些成分加起來形成原訊號。

cues.en: Now, different ICA algorithms work differently.
cues.zh: 不同演算法方式不同。

cues.en: So this happens to be an example of what's called the JADE algorithm.
cues.zh: 這是 JADE 的例子。

cues.en: This is one of, I don't know how many ICA algorithms, there are maybe around a dozen or so.
cues.zh: 不知道總共有多少 ICA 演算法，也許十幾種。

cues.en: They all work kind of differently, they all key on different factors, but they all start from the same basic two assumptions.
cues.zh: 做法不同、關注因素不同，但都從兩個基本假設出發。

cues.en: Real signals, true signals, are non-Gaussian-distributed and random mixtures of signals are Gaussian-distributed.
cues.zh: 真正訊號非高斯，隨機混合是高斯。

cues.en: Okay, so I'm going to give you an overview of the algorithm for ICA.
cues.zh: 概述演算法。

cues.en: So I started here by simulating data, and then what I did is mix these two data together.
cues.zh: 先模擬資料，再混合兩組資料。

cues.en: So this was like the true ground truth, original data.
cues.zh: 這是原始真實資料。

cues.en: And then I created this dataset of two variables, x and y.
cues.zh: 再建立 X、Y 兩個變數。

cues.en: You can see that these two variables are correlated with each other, but they look a little bit different from the original vectors s and t or the original axes s and t.
cues.zh: 彼此相關，但與原本 S、T 向量或座標軸有點不同。

cues.en: And that's because of the way that I combine the data.
cues.zh: 因為資料組合方式。

cues.en: So here, the data get randomly mixed together and this is what they look like.
cues.zh: 隨機混合後像這樣。

cues.en: This is what we measure with our sensors, or questionnaires, or, you know, whatever is the thing we're measuring.
cues.zh: 是感測器、問卷或其他量測實際得到的。

cues.en: So the first step is to whiten the data,, and that removes all of the co-variances.
cues.zh: 第一步白化，移除所有共變異。

cues.en: Whitening is a step that's actually done by PCA, and it essentially involves converting the co-variance matrix into a matrix that has all zeros on the off diagonal.
cues.zh: 透過 PCA 白化，基本上把共變異數矩陣變成非對角線全為 0 的矩陣。

cues.en: So all of the correlations across all the different variables are set to be zero.
cues.zh: 不同變數間相關全設為 0。

cues.en: And that's what...
cues.zh: 也就是。

cues.en: Then you see this example, this whitened version of this example here.
cues.zh: 這是這份資料白化後的版本。

cues.en: So we still see that there is a relationship between the variables, and that's important because what ICA is gonna look for is these relationships.
cues.zh: 仍有變數關係，很重要，ICA 要找它。

cues.en: But the data themselves have been removed of any correlation.
cues.zh: 但資料已移除所有相關。

cues.en: So the correlation between PC1 and PC2 is zero, of course, by definition of how principal components analysis work, as I explained in the previous lecture.
cues.zh: PC1 與 PC2 零相關，按 PCA 定義，上一堂解釋過。

cues.en: Okay, now, if we look at the histograms of PC1 and PC2, this is what those two distributions look like.
cues.zh: 看 PC1、PC2 的直方圖，兩分布像這樣。

cues.en: So PC1 actually does look a little bit Gaussian.
cues.zh: PC1 有點高斯。

cues.en: A true Gaussian would be a little bit, you know, a little bit gentler here on the down slope.
cues.zh: 真正高斯的下降斜坡會更平緩。

cues.en: But this one looks sort of Gaussian-ish, and you can see why, you know, there's a large clustering of data points here in the middle, and then there's fewer and fewer data points
cues.zh: 但這個看起來有點像高斯分布，你可以看出原因：中央聚集許多資料點，接著資料點越來越少，

cues.en: as we get further away from the center of this axis here.
cues.zh: 離軸中心愈遠，點愈少。

cues.en: And then we see PC2.
cues.zh: 再看 PC2。

cues.en: This one definitely already looks non-Gaussian.
cues.zh: 肯定已是非高斯。

cues.en: So we have a large clustering of data here.
cues.zh: 這裡大量資料。

cues.en: The clustering tapers down as we get higher, and there are zero data points below here.
cues.zh: 往上逐漸減少，下面完全沒有。

cues.en: So this is the histogram of PC2.
cues.zh: 是 PC2 直方圖。

cues.en: Now, ICA is going to look at this data and it's gonna look at these distributions, and it's gonna say, "Well, I like PC2.
cues.zh: ICA 會看分布，說：「喜歡 PC2。

cues.en: This looks non-Gaussian, this looks great.
cues.zh: 不是高斯，很棒。

cues.en: But, PC1 doesn't look so great.
cues.zh: 但 PC1 不太好。

cues.en: That looks too much like a Gaussian.
cues.zh: 太像高斯。

cues.en: So then I," speaking on behalf of ICA, "I'm going to try to rotate these axes and shift around the data
cues.zh: 所以我要，」這是代 ICA 發言，「旋轉座標軸、移動資料，

cues.en: in order to make this distribution look even less Gaussian."
cues.zh: 讓分布更不像高斯。」

cues.en: Okay, but you do see that although the strict linear dependencies are removed, there is still shared information preserved in this dataset.
cues.zh: 雖然移除嚴格線性相依，仍保有共同資訊。

cues.en: Now, this is the shared information that ICA is going to pick up on.
cues.zh: 就是 ICA 要捕捉的。

cues.en: So then the idea is to rotate these two axes.
cues.zh: 接著旋轉兩軸。

cues.en: We have the PC1 axis and the PC2 axis.
cues.zh: PC1 與 PC2。

cues.en: And these get rotated to minimize this amount of shared information.
cues.zh: 旋轉以最小化共同資訊。

cues.en: Now, this is where ICA and PCA really start to diverge because PCA is only an orthogonal rotation of the data.
cues.zh: 這是 ICA 與 PCA 開始大幅不同之處，PCA 只是正交旋轉。

cues.en: So with PCA, you saw in the example two videos ago, I guess, or the previous lecture, and you see that again here.
cues.zh: 兩支之前，或者上一堂的例子，以及這裡，都看到。

cues.en: So with PCA, we're not changing the orientations of the axes with respect to each other.
cues.zh: PCA 不改變兩軸相對方向。

cues.en: We're just rotating all of the data in this data space.
cues.zh: 只在資料空間旋轉全部資料。

cues.en: Now, ICA, on the other hand, is more flexible than that.
cues.zh: ICA 更有彈性。

cues.en: So ICA is actually going to take these two vectors and rotate them obliquely and independently of each other.
cues.zh: 可以各自獨立、斜向旋轉兩向量。

cues.en: So it's actually taking this V shape here and opening it up, it's spreading out this V.
cues.zh: 把 V 形打開、展寬。

cues.en: It's like if you imagine putting your palms together as if you're clapping and then you open up your fingers, you spread your fingers apart from each other
cues.zh: 像把手掌合起來拍手，再張開手指，讓手指分開，

cues.en: while leaving the heels of your hands touching each other.
cues.zh: 掌根仍接觸。

cues.en: So that's what's going on here.
cues.zh: 就是這樣。

cues.en: So ICA took these two directions and opened them up to create this independent component space.
cues.zh: 把兩方向打開，建立獨立成分空間。

cues.en: And now, look what that did to the distribution.
cues.zh: 看看分布變化。

cues.en: So the PC2 actually is still a bit preserved here.
cues.zh: PC2 這裡仍有點保留。

cues.en: And then IC1, which used to be PC1, that really became strongly non-Gaussian distributions.
cues.zh: 原本 PC1 的 IC1，變成非常強的非高斯分布。

cues.en: So now we have two distributions that are really, really non-Gaussian.
cues.zh: 現在兩分布都非常非高斯。

cues.en: Okay, and that is a bit of a sort of quick overview of how ICA works.
cues.zh: 這是快速概觀。

cues.en: So this is a slide that's taken from a different course, and what I mainly want to illustrate here is that different decomposition methods
cues.zh: 這張來自另一門課，主要說明不同分解方法，

cues.en: work based on different maximization functions.
cues.zh: 使用不同的最大化函數。

cues.en: They make different assumptions about the data, and they have different kinds of output statistics.
cues.zh: 不同資料假設、不同輸出統計。

cues.en: Now, I didn't really talk about GED, this method here, but that part doesn't matter.
cues.zh: 沒有談 GED，但不重要。

cues.en: The main point that I want to impart on you here is that there are different dimension reduction procedures, and they're generally all going to work differently.
cues.zh: 我想傳達的重點是，降維程序有很多種，而它們一般都以不同方式運作。

cues.en: They're going to give you different results because they're looking for different things in the data, they're maximizing different features of the data, they make different assumptions
cues.zh: 結果不同，因為找不同東西、最大化不同資料特徵，對資料

cues.en: about the data and about the world, and they also provide different statistics.
cues.zh: 與世界有不同假設，也提供不同統計。

cues.en: So these different methods can give you quite different results.
cues.zh: 所以結果可能差很多。

cues.en: You'll also see examples of that in the code.
cues.zh: 程式也會看例子。

cues.en: So in this video, I introduced you to ICA, independent components analysis, and I gave a simplified overview of the assumptions of ICA and the basic framework
cues.zh: 這支介紹 ICA、獨立成分分析，簡述假設與基本架構，

cues.en: for how an ICA works on multi-variate datasets.
cues.zh: 如何處理多變量資料。

cues.en: I want to conclude this by showing these two pictures that I've shown earlier in this course.
cues.zh: 最後展示課程前面兩張圖。

cues.en: This was for PCA versus ICA on the same data, and this was for K-means versus OPTICS clustering on this same kind of, you know, happy/sad face dataset.
cues.zh: 同資料 PCA 對 ICA，以及笑臉、哭臉資料的 K-means 對 OPTICS。

cues.en: There's a more general point here, which is that clustering and dimension reduction and dealing with multi-variate data in general can be a little bit tricky.
cues.zh: 更一般的重點，是分群、降維與多變量資料處理，可能有點難。

cues.en: It's tempting to say, "Well, here's this really cool analysis that I read about, you know, I've watched a video on it, or I'd read about it on some data science blog.
cues.zh: 很容易想：「剛讀到很酷的分析，看過影片或資料科學部落格，

cues.en: So now, let me throw my data at it and see what happens."
cues.zh: 把資料丟進去看看吧。」

cues.en: So on the one hand, I do encourage exploring different methods and exploring your data, but on the other hand, I think it's important to appreciate
cues.zh: 一方面鼓勵探索方法與資料，但也要了解，

cues.en: that as you get further and further into statistics and you get into more sophisticated statistical and machine learning methods,
cues.zh: 統計愈深入，統計與機器學習方法愈精緻，

cues.en: the amount of uncertainty increases greatly.
cues.zh: 不確定性增加很多。

cues.en: And just the, you know, the ability to trust that the method is doing what's right for your data decreases sharply.
cues.zh: 相信方法會替資料做正確事情的能力，大幅下降。

cues.en: So when it comes to relatively simple, straightforward analyses like t-tests and correlations, regression analyses, as long as you're setting up the models correctly,
cues.zh: t 檢定、相關、迴歸等相對簡單分析，只要模型設對，

cues.en: you can trust the results, you're going to get decent results.
cues.zh: 可以信任結果，會得到不錯結果。

cues.en: But when we start to get to these more sophisticated methods, it's no longer the case that you can really just blindly assume that the method is going to do
cues.zh: 但開始使用這些更精密的方法時，就不能再盲目假設，這個方法會做出

cues.en: what's appropriate for your dataset.
cues.zh: 適合你的資料集的處理。

cues.en: So anytime you're applying clustering, dimension reduction, analyses, make sure you're thinking carefully about which methods you're applying, what are the assumptions
cues.zh: 做分群、降維時，仔細思考使用哪個方法、它對資料

cues.en: that those methods are making about your data, whether those assumptions are met in your data, and whether the output of those methods
cues.zh: 有什麼假設、資料是否符合，以及輸出

cues.en: is telling you what you would like to infer from the data.
cues.zh: 是否告訴你想從資料推論的事情。
